consensus_summary: Consensus treats the tower as context-dependent but primarily divine strength/protection/refuge (God as strong tower per Prov 18:10 and parallel Psalms), with common alternatives of human pride/rebellion (Babel) and watchfulness/vigilance; other senses (cost-counting, Siloam, allegory) are secondary.
book_summary: Book defines the tower as the stronghold raised by a Name around its house, uniting refuge, watchtower, and lighthouse; a strong tower is an intact Name protecting its people, an unfinished tower a Name begun without depth to endure cost, and a fallen tower a broken/emptied/judged covenant stronghold.
consensus_core_identification: Divine protection/refuge (primary) or human pride or prophetic watchfulness (common alternatives), each as separate contextual senses.
book_core_identification: Stronghold raised by a Name around its house (refuge + watch + light in one), with states of intact/unfinished/fallen Name or covenant.
boundary_disagreement: Book unifies refuge/watch/pride/cost/fall under one Name-stronghold framework and adds lighthouse function plus explicit intact/unfinished/fallen typology; consensus keeps the senses separate and context-bound without that synthesis or the light pillar images.
material_contradiction: None; the book does not deny the refuge, Babel, watch, or cost senses but re-frames and conditions them.
rationale: Minimum cores share the protective/refuge referent (anchored in Prov 18:10) and retain Babel, watch, cost, and fall as cases; the book therefore does not replace the central identification. It does, however, materially narrow and re-specify by requiring the tower to be a Name-raised stronghold that simultaneously functions as refuge/watch/lighthouse and by partitioning all instances into intact/unfinished/fallen states (drawing Matt 13 rootlessness into unfinished and Siloam/Babel into fallen). This is boundary refinement plus partial reclassification, not core contradiction or pure novelty.
strongest_objection: The synthesis of pillar-of-fire/cloud and Isa 4 defence imagery as ‘lighthouse-tower,’ plus the mapping of stony-ground discipleship onto unfinished towers, is an over-extension not licensed by the plain texts or by any consensus strand.
